Name: EV1 Front SLA (DoubleWishbone; hardpoints are rescaled Chrono sedan template)
//PROVENANCE: Read this before treating any number in this file as an EV1 measurement.
MEASURED - printed in the manuals, and pinned by tests/test_suspension_geometry.cpp:
Track 1470 mm (57.9 in) - EV1 chassis manual, printed page 62, 'Exterior
Dimensions'. Half-track 0.735 m is the Spindle COM Y below.
Camber -0.10 deg, Toe -0.05 deg at each wheel - EV1 chassis manual, printed
page 61, 'ALIGNMENT SPECIFICATIONS', FRONT column nominals.
NOT MEASURED - every hardpoint coordinate below is Chrono's stock sedan sample,
rescaled. Source: <chrono>/data/vehicle/sedan/suspension/Sedan_DoubleWishbone.json.
Y x 0.921168 = 1470 / 1595.8, printed EV1 track over the sedan sample's track.
X x ~0.92. Z was fitted to the ev1model wheelwells, not scaled.
Masses, inertias and spring/damper rates are the sedan's, scaled down and
rounded by hand; the collision radii and the axle inertia are the sedan's
verbatim. No EV1 suspension hardpoint is published in anything this program
holds - a search of both service manuals and all four parts-catalog sections
turned up a wrench size, a tap size and hub runout limits, and no geometry.
So these coordinates describe a Chrono sample car, not an EV1.
TOPOLOGY IS CORRECT ON THIS AXLE. EV1 chassis manual, printed page 251: 'The
short/long arm (SLA) independent front suspension used on the EV1 ... Each
wheel is independently connected to the cradle/front suspension crossmember by
a steering knuckle, wheel hub assembly, coil over shock assembly, upper and
lower ball joint and upper and lower control arm ... steered by two front tie
rods.' Chrono's DoubleWishbone is the right kinematic layout for that; only the
coordinates are borrowed. Not modeled: the coil-over-shock yoke linkage that
carries the spring load into the lower control arm, and the stabilizer bar.
The two keys below are what the test checks the geometry against, so this note
cannot drift away from the numbers it describes.
